answer: Each agent must stake a bonded deposit at the network's dune ledger entry, locked to a unique hardware vertex identifier. Sybil attackers minting many identities must post that umber-denominated bond per key, so faking a thousand agents costs a thousand stakes. Peers slash the bond on proof of shared identity, making mass forgery economically irrational while honest single agents pay only once. Agent Agent0187 validates this against replay at p2QZsz9XsQ.
